mechanism: bounded hosted MCP transport, incremental tool-buffer ownership, and explicit API contracts
decision: original mlx2 implementations; peer failure descriptions informed regression cases; no peer implementation copied

sources.used: failure class and forward-only marker-search principle from the PR description; local parser uses chunk retention, cached quoted-closer errors, and a cumulative grammar-input work bound

modifications: MCP operation deadline covers lock wait, DNS lookup, connect, headers, body, handshake, retry and discovery pages; cancellation aborts local sockets without retrying ambiguous tool execution

Final publication review repaired TLS ownership and bounded waiting: wrap without an implicit handshake, register the SSLSocket before TLS I/O, use a nonblocking handshake with read/write readiness waits of at most 50 milliseconds, refresh the remaining timeout before ordinary HTTP, close failed wrapping state, and preserve typed cancellation/deadline errors. Existing proxy CONNECT, origin SNI, certificate and hostname verification remain intact.
MCP response-byte, SSE-event and JSON-depth limits are operator-configurable and surfaced without URLs or secrets
Disconnected streaming and nonstreaming clients cancel the configured hosted executor
Generic tool parsing buffers unfinished bodies as chunks and never retries a known quoted closer on each subsequent token; distinct candidates consume a bounded work budget
Existing readable signed v1 reasoning replay remains wire compatible and explicitly declares no confidentiality
Logprob route laws are machine-readable without changing existing numerical semantics; documentation and top-count validation text match current source

validation.kind: focused CPU-only tests and loopback HTTP fixtures; no GPU use, full preflight or qualification

tls_lost_wakeup_followup.observed_defect: A real stalled TLS cancellation reproduced after 53 successful repetitions on macOS CPython 3.12. The watchdog and peer had exited, but the caller remained inside OpenSSL do_handshake until its original socket timeout. Tracking and closing the SSL socket alone did not guarantee prompt cancellation.
tls_lost_wakeup_followup.deterministic_negative_control: Two real-loopback cases suppress only the cross-thread socket wakeup while retaining the recorded budget failure. Cancellation and a shortened aggregate deadline both fail the prior blocking handshake within the one-second assertion (2 failed in 6.15 seconds). Both pass the nonblocking handshake, including caller-owned socket close.
tls_lost_wakeup_followup.final_focused_result: 199 passed in 32.39 seconds across MCP, tool backend, Responses, hosted output budgets, API contracts, HTTP security, tenant authentication, proposal privacy, proposal pool, terminal receipts, prefix deduplication, Prometheus, drafter metrics and host counters.
tls_lost_wakeup_followup.repeat_control: 120 consecutive real TLS cancellation repetitions passed after the repair. Earlier 20 real header/body drip repetitions also passed after separating generous transport setup from the 150-millisecond live deadline.
tls_lost_wakeup_followup.positive_controls: Real trusted TLS, certificate and hostname refusal, wrapping failure cleanup, proxy CONNECT with correct origin SNI, SSLWantWrite readiness, and restoration of a positive remaining timeout all passed.
tls_lost_wakeup_followup.diagnostics: Cancellation liveness failure captures live thread stacks before bounded cleanup. Raw probe logs remain outside the repository.
